crowd.name: Crowded trading
crowd.desc: How heavily the stock is traded (60-day turnover). On NEPSE the most-traded stocks underperform and quiet ones outperform: the strongest pattern in the data.

calm.name: Low volatility
calm.desc: Calm, steady stocks (60-day volatility). Helps avoid the wild names; lags in euphoric bull runs.

surge.name: Turnover surge
surge.desc: Is the stock suddenly trading far more than its own 1-year normal? A surge of attention tends to be followed by weaker returns.

pressure.name: Closing pressure
pressure.desc: Closing above the day's average price (VWAP). Late-day pushes tend to unwind.

nolottery.name: No lottery spikes
nolottery.desc: Stocks WITHOUT a recent huge one-day jump. Spiky 'lottery' stocks tend to disappoint later.

high52.name: Near 52-week high
high52.desc: Stocks close to their 1-year high tend to keep doing slightly better.

chasing.name: Circuit chasing
chasing.desc: How often the stock hit the +10% upper circuit in the last 20 days. Frequent circuit-hitters tend to fall back.

model_history.summary: 8 generic signals (momentum, sector rotation, ...), 10 stocks, 20-day review, NEPSE 50-day trend filter.
First NEPSE-specific model: anti closing-pressure, calm stocks, circuit filters, 12 stocks, 40-day review, stop-losses, bear-market cash filter.

Built around NEPSE's strongest pattern: crowded, heavily traded stocks lag and quiet ones lead. 16 stocks, each reviewed every 60 days, no stop-losses (they destroyed value), no market timing, realistic market-impact costs, fixed research weights.
